tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Create a Jinja2 environment with configurable settings. loader: A Jinja2 loader instance for loading templates, extensions: List of Jinja2 extensions to use, autoescape: Enable XML/HTML autoescaping. Example: create_environment(autoescape=True) -> Environment instance.

tools.name: create_template
tools.description: Compile a template from a source string using a Jinja2 environment. source: The template source code as a string, e.g. '{{ name }}' -> Template object serialized as string.

tools.name: render_template
tools.description: Render a template with provided variables and return the result as a string. template: The template string to render, e.g. 'Hello {{ name }}!' -> 'Hello World!'. context: The context variables to use for rendering, e.g. {'name': 'World'}.

samples.template: {% for item in items %}{{ item }}{% endfor %}

tools.name: tokenize_template
tools.description:
Lex the template source code and return a generator of tokens.
    
    Each token is returned as a tuple in the form (lineno, token_type, value).
    This can be useful for extension development and debugging templates.
    
    Args:
        source (str): The template source code to lex
        name (str | None): Name of the template (optional)
        filename (str | None): Filename of the template (optional)
    
    Returns:
        List[Tuple[int, str, str]]: List of tokens as (line_number, token_type, value) tuples
    
    Example:
        >>> tokenize_template("Hello {{ name }}!")
        [(1, 'name', 'Hello '), (1, 'variable_begin', '{{'), (1, 'name', 'name'), (1, 'variable_end', '}}'), (1, 'name', '!')]

tools.name: create_dict_loader
tools.description: Create a Jinja2 loader that loads templates from a Python dictionary. mapping: A dictionary mapping template names to template source strings, e.g. {'index.html': 'Hello {{ name }}'}.

tools.name: create_overlay_environment
tools.description:
Create a new Jinja2 environment that shares data with the current one but overrides specific settings.
    
    Args:
        block_start_string: The string marking the start of a block
        block_end_string: The string marking the end of a block
        variable_start_string: The string marking the start of a variable
        variable_end_string: The string marking the end of a variable
    
    Returns:
        A dictionary representation of the new environment, or None if no parameters provided
    
    Example:
        >>> create_overlay_environment(variable_start_string='[[')
        {'variable_start_string': '[['}

tools.name: clear_jinja_caches
tools.description: Clear internal caches for environments and lexers to free memory. This is useful when measuring memory consumption.

tools.name: iterate_tokens
tools.description: Tokenize a Jinja2 template source and return tokens as an iterator. source: The Jinja2 template source code to tokenize, name: Name of the template, filename: Filename of the template, state: Initial parsing state ('root', 'variable', or 'block'). Example: iterate_tokens('Hello {{ name }}', 'test') -> iterator of tokens.

tools.name: join_markup
tools.description: Concatenation that escapes if necessary and converts to string. sequence: A sequence of values to concatenate, e.g. ['hello', 'world'] -> 'helloworld'.

tools.name: join_strings
tools.description: Convert arguments to strings and concatenate them. items: sequence of items to convert to strings and concatenate, e.g. [1, 2, 3] -> '123'.

tools.name: describe_token_expression
tools.description: Returns a human-readable description of a token expression used in the lexer. expr: A token expression string, e.g. 'name:foo' -> 'foo'.
